roomAnchor.prompt:
Use all five supplied images ONLY as the EXACT ROOM, ARCHITECTURE, FURNITURE, COLOUR AND LIGHTING reference for a new photorealistic campaign. Create a single EMPTY ROOM anchor photograph, PORTRAIT 4:5, target 1122x1402.
Preserve this recognizable same living room: blue evening light through window and curtains on the LEFT, navy-blue fabric sofa with a thick cream-and-navy knitted throw and burnt orange cushion across middle, tall dark honey-oak BOOKCASE filled with books and a small globe on RIGHT, trailing green houseplants over shelves, warm amber floor/table lamp with woven cream shade at right behind sofa, substantial warm worn wooden coffee table dominating foreground. Deep blue shadows, amber warm practical light, restrained cyan reflected highlights. The intimate cozy evening room must match the references rather than become a different generic living room. Maintain the arrangement and character of the furniture.
REMOVE every person, mascot, paper, smartphone, magnifier, fictional treasure prop, graphic, text, logo, glowing path and advertisement copy. We need just an empty real photographic room and clear wooden tabletop. Leave top approximately 20–24% as usable dark room wall/curtain backdrop for later advertising lettering, but keep this atmospheric and continuous, not a flat colour panel. Show more tabletop and surrounding room than the close-up reference photographs: wide 35mm editorial interior photograph, believable real wood/fabric/plant detail, ordinary beautiful home, subtle film texture, photorealistic NOT CGI, NOT painterly, NOT hyperprocessed. No text or borders. Full-bleed canvas.

baseScenePrompt:
Produce a new FULL-BLEED PHOTOREALISTIC 4:5 lifestyle advertising photograph for Pixelkovia, a family detective adventure played with printed A4 clues and one shared smartphone. Image 1 is the LOCKED ROOM / LIGHTING reference: preserve that EXACT same room, furniture layout and colour atmosphere. Image 2 is ONLY a reference for the humans' convincing photographic skin/hair/anatomy and natural expressions; do NOT copy its close framing, generic room, text, papers or screen.
ROOM: keep the recognizable navy sofa, blue evening window on LEFT, amber lamp and tall warm oak BOOKCASE with books/globe on RIGHT, trailing plants, knitted throw and orange cushion. Same amber-blue cozy evening atmosphere as Image 1, believable practical illumination. Preserve this room, not a different home. Real wood, textiles, gentle film grain; amber and blue lights on skin must be subtle and physically plausible, never orange plastic faces, airbrushing, cinematic CGI or glossy AI stock-photo skin.
FRAMING / SALES PRIORITY: zoom OUT about 25–30 percent from a close-up family advertisement. Show MORE of the room, table and activity. The GAME and the real materials will be the main subject; people support the scene. People's heads should be visibly SMALLER than in Image 2; the family sits further from camera, in the MIDDLE DISTANCE. Foreground wooden table occupies roughly lower 40–45% of image. Leave top 22–27% as atmospheric dark room/curtain/wall for later lettering, with real room detail visible; not a flat navy panel. Show generous tabletop at both sides for later tiny mascots. The photo fills every canvas edge.
PRODUCT COMPOSITING SLOTS: show EXACTLY ONE clean completely BLANK WHITE A4 sheet on table, its top edge approximately at 64–68% image height, visible printed area extending down toward 89% height and the rest continuing beyond bottom canvas. Leave it physically clear and in focus. At lower RIGHT show ONE real dark portrait smartphone lying on same table, visibly large (about 18% canvas width, 22% height) with ALL FOUR inner-screen corners visible, completely uniform near-black BLANK screen for exact original game insert. Aim phone screen top around 63–67% height, bottom no lower than 88% height. No hands across its screen. Hands may point NEXT TO the paper but not cover its central area. A simple pencil on empty wood is okay.
ABSOLUTELY NO other papers, round decoders, wheels, puzzle cut-outs, maps, treasure props, graphics, writing, letters, numbers, screen interfaces, logos, headlines, mascots or magical trails. The original actual game materials and small approved mascots will be added separately. Do not invent game components. Anatomically correct natural hands, subtle honest expressions, no exaggerated laughter or giant portrait faces. No borders, watermark or text.
